slot.brief: Set up and compute the area between a parabola and a line/second parabola using intersection points as limits.

stem: The area enclosed by the parabola $y=x^2$ and the line $y=2x+3$ is

verdicts.working: Intersections: x² = 2x + 3 gives x = −1, 3. The line lies above the parabola between them, so area = ∫₋₁³(2x + 3 − x²) dx = 32/3.

working:
$x^2=2x+3\implies x=-1,3$
$A=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{3}(2x+3-x^2)\,dx$
$=\left[x^2+3x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{3}=9-\left(-\dfrac{5}{3}\right)=\dfrac{32}{3}$

Independent check: Intersections: x² = 2x + 3 gives x = −1, 3. The line lies above the parabola between them, so area = ∫₋₁³(2x + 3 − x²) dx = 32/3.
